messages:
maya_support: noticing a sharp spike in 504s from hosted API around 07:12 UTC, p95->p99 tail timeouts. multiple customers reporting errors. mounting backlog in request queue. attaching quick timeline.
owen_sre: which gateway/errors exactly? 504s from frontend or 5xx from runtime? any tenant skew?
maya_support: frontend gateway returning 504. logs show 'request deadline exceeded' + downstream batcher queue wait >10s. tenant T-842 had a large ramp.
anna_runtime: we've got continuous-batching backlog growth. KV cache hits steady, but batcher dequeue latency spiked. looks like queue depth limit reached on some hosts.
lina_eng: can you dump the batcher queue lengths (per-host) and the continuous_batch_window metric? also any recent rollout?
maya_support: pulling graphs -> grafana link (omitted). short snippets:
```
batcher.dequeue_latency_p50: 120ms -> 3.2s
batcher.dequeue_pending: 8 -> 120
continuous_batch_window_ms: 20 -> 120
```
deploy-bot: deployment "hosted-frontends" rolled out 07:05 UTC to 07:08 UTC (v2026.3.4)
owen_sre: hmm rollout might have tightened batching defaults. anna — did runtime change default window/queue behavior in that release?
anna_runtime: yes, default continuous_batch_window lowered to 10ms in v2026.3.4 to improve latency normally. unintended side-effect: under sudden ingress surge, batcher spins and queue depth climbs because early_reject wasn't enabled yet.
jeff_support: affected customer on ticket #2541. they reported end-user facing timeouts and a 30% error rate for a 10-min window. they provided a repro curl:  
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-open-3b","prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
maya_support: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable early_reject at gateway (reject when queue_depth > threshold) 2) temporarily increase queue depth limit on hosts 3) route heavy tenants to warm model-variant or smaller model 4) revert batching param change. want quick wins.
owen_sre: priority: reduce customer impact now. plan: enable early_reject on frontends, set threshold to 40, flip continuous_batch_window back to 50ms for hosted-prod, and scale up dedicated pool by +2 nodes if autoscale will cooperate. anna, can you toggle flags?
anna_runtime: prepared flag changes. command to flip:
```
redwood-opsctl set feature early_reject=true --env=hosted-prod --scope=frontends
redwood-opsctl set feature continuous_batch_window_ms=50 --env=hosted-prod
```
anna_runtime: applying now, will monitor p50/p95.
owen_sre: also adding a temporary rule in gateway to route tenant T-842 to model-variant rwd-open-3b-warm which has shorter decode p95.
lina_eng: caution: increasing queue depth buys time but increases tail latency if batcher backlog stays. early_reject recommended.
maya_support: notify customer that we have mitigation in progress, ETA 5-10m. jeff, can you patch ticket?
jeff_support: on it. messaging: "We've identified a queuing backlog caused by a recent batching change; apply mitigation now, will follow up with root cause and timeline." :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: feature flip: early_reject=true applied to frontends at 07:21:40 UTC
anna_runtime: continuous_batch_window_ms rolled back to 50ms at 07:22:05 UTC
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ACKNOWLEDGED by owen_sre at 07:22:10 UTC
nowen_sre: initial metrics look better — dequeue_pending per-host dropping from 120 -> ~20 in ~2m. p95 timeouts down to baseline.
maya_support: customer confirmed errors subsided, ticket updated. major impact window ~07:12-07:24 UTC.
lina_eng: postmortem action items: 1) add guardrail in release pipeline to prevent batch-window reductions without enabling early_reject 2) add a runtime metric alert for continuous_batch_window vs pending_count 3) document tenant isolation knobs and add support runbook.
ownen_sre: agree. also add automated rollback if dequeue_pending > 100 for >2m after rollout.
maya_support: thanks everyone — I'll draft a short incident summary and assign follow-ups. closing updates in 1h.
jeff_support: will share customer note once summary is ready. :white_check_mark:
